observation_summary: The Joda-Time library was incorrectly mapping several time zone IDs (e.g., 'MET', 'WET', 'ECT') to wrong geographical regions, causing tests to fail when comparing expected IDs with actual resolved IDs.
hypothesis: The internal mapping table used for backward compatibility in DateTimeZone was initialized with incorrect string values for several time zone keys.
prediction: The code will contain a static map initialization block where the values associated with keys like 'MET', 'WET', and 'ECT' are set to incorrect time zone identifiers.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows a direct modification of the key-value pairs in the 'map' object within the DateTimeZone class, correcting the mappings to the expected values.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic case of incorrect data initialization. The system relies on a lookup table (a Map) to resolve legacy time zone IDs. The values in this map were hardcoded incorrectly, and the fix simply updates these values to the correct ones. This does not involve changing the algorithm, adding guards, or modifying interfaces; it is purely an assignment/initialization correction.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the removal of incorrect mappings (e.g., map.put("MET", "Asia/Tehran")) and the addition of correct ones (e.g., map.put("MET", "CET")).
The failing test 'testForID_String_old' confirms that the system was returning 'Europe/London' instead of the expected 'WET' for the 'WET' key.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The logic for looking up the time zone is correct; only the data being looked up was wrong.
This is a data correction, not a design-level capability gap.
